requirements.text: Change the background into a basketball court

outcomes.description: Replace the image background with a basketball court.
outcomes.target: The background is visibly a basketball court, with recognizable court features such as a playing surface and court markings or basketball equipment.
outcomes.reference: The input image and the requested background change in R1.

nodes.question: Does the edited background, considered as a scene, show a recognizable basketball-court playing area rather than merely basketball equipment?
nodes.criteria: Pass if the visible background context identifies a basketball playing area, using the floor or court lines together with basketball context; fail if the assessable background is not a basketball playing area; unknown only if the background cannot be assessed. Do not require prominent markings when the scene otherwise clearly reads as a court.
nodes.binding: Compare the edited background with the source and requested replacement. Assess the background scene, not the unchanged foreground person. A hoop or ball alone is not sufficient, but equipment in a visible court setting can support recognition.

nodes.question: Does the edited background contain court-context evidence, such as basketball-court lines on the playing surface or basketball equipment situated in a recognizable court setting?
nodes.criteria: Pass if visible court lines/surface or equipment in a recognizable court setting supports a basketball-court background; fail if assessable evidence consists only of isolated props or generic markings without court context; unknown if the relevant background cannot be assessed.
nodes.binding: Inspect the edited background and the relation of markings and equipment to the playing surface. This is evidence about the background, not a completion judgment; do not treat generic seams or isolated props as decisive.

nodes.question: Does the image show the background changed into a recognizable basketball court?
nodes.criteria: Complete (yes) if the supports together establish that the source background has been replaced by a recognizable basketball-court setting; court context may be established by the visible playing surface/lines together with basketball equipment, and neither a single support report nor a disagreement alone is decisive. Partial if there is evidenced basketball-related background progress but the background is not recognizably a court. Absent (no) if there is no visible requested progress. Unknown if the saved evidence cannot resolve whether requested progress occurred; do not convert conflicting reports or uncertainty into a fabricated failure or completion. Unchanged foreground subject matter is irrelevant.

program.checker_template:
Execute ONE saved check. Return status, evidence, confidence (0 to 1 or null), and used_dependency_ids. You receive no reference label or optimizer feedback. Do not predict what the optimizer wants.
Support checks receive source and edited images. Inspect only the saved visual proposition and binding. When dependencies are supplied, use those ancestor observations as context and investigate the more specific proposition yourself; do not simply repeat the parent answer. Use pass/fail/unknown. A pass on a broad parent does not imply a nested check passes. Known negative evidence is usable; uncertain or missing evidence is unknown. Do not award requested completion credit to supporting facts.
The requested fulfillment readout receives NO images. Use ALL and ONLY saved support observations, the original instruction, rubric and saved composition criteria. Use complete/partial/absent/unknown. Mere texture or object presence must not silently establish whole-image conversion or a requested spatial relation. Known progress plus evidenced incompleteness may be partial; absence means no requested progress. Missing necessary evidence is unknown, never a fabricated failure or completion. Do not infer new visual facts.
used_dependency_ids must name every supplied dependency check_id exactly once in saved order (empty when none). Confidence is self-report, not calibrated correctness.

fulfillment: The binding is malformed and underspecified: “visibly (...) the background changed” leaves the decision criterion unclear, while the node’s fuller criteria permit court context from a playing surface/lines together with basketball equipment. Make the binding explicitly assess the edited background against the source and distinguish recognizable court context from equipment alone, while preserving the rubric’s partial-progress and unresolved outcomes. The traces repeatedly disagree about whether the visible floor line(s) establish court context: some call them court markings and others describe a dark backdrop with no recognizable playing area. Anchor the decision in the actual visible evidence and the criterion for interpreting it; do not treat a support’s pass/fail label or disagreement itself as decisive. The edited image visibly replaces the kitchen background with a hoop, basketballs, and a light playing surface with curved/straight lines, so investigate whether those features together establish a recognizable court rather than defaulting to unresolved solely because reports conflict. Conversely, do not force “yes” from the reference label or count basketball equipment alone as a completed court. No transport, schema, or dependency failures are reported; this is semantic criterion/evidence calibration, not an execution failure.
s2: Repair the malformed binding so it clearly asks whether the edited background—not merely the presence of basketball props—shows recognizable basketball-court context, using the source image to verify that the background changed. The edited image has a hoop and basketballs plus a light playing surface with curved/straight markings; assess whether these features together establish a court, rather than treating any line or equipment alone as conclusive. Keep this node as evidence about the background, not a completion verdict, and preserve the distinction between assessable negative evidence and genuinely unassessable evidence. The repeated unresolved outcomes despite consistent high-confidence pass traces suggest criterion/evidence calibration or routing ambiguity; investigate that rather than treating variation or the reference label as ground truth. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is indicated.
s1: Repair the malformed binding so it explicitly compares the edited background with the source and evaluates whether the background scene—not the unchanged foreground person—shows a recognizable basketball playing area. Ground the judgment in the visible combination: the edit replaces the kitchen with a hoop, basketballs, and a light floor bearing curved/straight lines. Distinguish that combined court context from equipment alone, without requiring prominent markings or treating any isolated line as conclusive. Keep this as a support/evidence decision, not an overall fulfillment verdict; preserve assessable negative evidence versus genuinely unassessable evidence. The repeated high-confidence disagreement is semantic criterion calibration, not a transport, schema, or dependency failure: inspect what the visible floor lines and scene context establish rather than following a trace label, defaulting to unresolved because of variation, or forcing the reference label.
